slots.headline: A waterfront concert run, a War of 1812 weekend, and coastal Delaware's first Dockside & IRM fishing tournament
slots.note: The week opens with back-to-back Melvin Seals & JGB shows at Rocking the Docks in Lewes and a ranger-led hike across the Indian River Inlet Bridge, builds to Historic Lewes' 'Under Enemy Guns' living-history weekend (Aug. 15–16) and a stacked run of free Bandstand concerts in Rehoboth, and closes with the first-ever Dockside & IRM Classic fishing tournament at Indian River Marina (Aug. 22–23).

slots.headline: Fowler Beach stays closed through October for nesting shorebirds
slots.note: At Prime Hook National Wildlife Refuge, Fowler Beach remains closed to protect federally threatened piping plovers and state-endangered least terns; it's scheduled to reopen October 1. The rest of the refuge's trails remain open sunrise to sunset.

slots.headline: Segregated Sands: the Jim Crow-era history behind Delaware's beaches
slots.note: The Zwaanendael Museum in Lewes hosts 'Segregated Sands,' an exhibit on the Black American experience at Delaware's segregated beaches during the Jim Crow era, alongside an oral-history initiative inviting community members to share their own stories. Free admission; open Tuesday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–4:15 p.m.

slots.headline: Why the Cedar Islands matter more than they look
slots.note: The marsh islands along Delaware Seashore's Cedar Island Water Trail are active nesting habitat for osprey, laughing gulls, herring and great black-backed gulls, Forster's and common terns, and multiple heron species — worth knowing before paddling the 2.8-mile loop, which is geared toward experienced kayakers given heat, wind, and tide.

slots.headline: Beach Plum Island: Delaware's only 'wilderness beach'
slots.note: A 129-acre state nature preserve on an undeveloped barrier spit north of Lewes — the only beach in the Delaware State Parks system left in a wilderness state. Open March through December for hiking, surf fishing, and wildlife viewing on marked trails only; the southern half stays closed year-round to protect it.

slots.headline: When the Royal Navy blockaded Lewes
slots.note: This weekend's 'Under Enemy Guns' living-history event revisits 1813, when Commodore John P. Beresford's British squadron shelled Lewes during the War of 1812 — the town's most-told maritime siege story, reenacted with musket volleys and boat drills on the Lewes-Rehoboth Canal.
